cards.title: If you are in danger right now
cards.body: If you feel unsafe, contact your local emergency number straight away. This app gives general safety information; it is not a substitute for help from the police or a trained advocate.

cards.title: Use a safer device to get help
cards.body: If someone may be watching this phone, look up help on a device they can't see — a friend's phone, a library or work computer — and in a private browser window. What you type here could be read.

cards.title: Trust what you notice
cards.body: If the person seems to know things they shouldn't — where you were, who you messaged — that is worth taking seriously, even if a scan finds nothing. Spyware can hide, and control doesn't always need an app.

cards.title: Don't change your routine suddenly
cards.body: If you think you're being monitored, acting differently all at once can signal that you know. Keep to your normal pattern while you plan your next steps with someone you trust.

cards.title: Write down what's happening
cards.body: Note the dates and details of anything that makes you uneasy. A record helps an advocate, the police or a lawyer understand the pattern later.

cards.title: Removing spyware can tip the person off
cards.body: When monitoring software is removed, the person watching often notices — the alerts stop. If they are someone who could become dangerous, that moment can be risky. Plan removal with a domestic-abuse advocate before you act.

cards.title: Save the proof before you clean up
cards.body: Export your evidence timeline and take screenshots first. Once an app is removed, the proof it was there can be gone, and you may need it for the police, a court or your phone company.

cards.title: Have a safety plan ready
cards.body: Decide where you'll be and who you'll be with when you make changes, and have a way to call for help. A local domestic-abuse service can help you build a plan that fits your situation.

cards.title: Change passwords from a safe device
cards.body: Assume your passwords may be known. From a device the person hasn't touched, change the passwords for your email, cloud account and messaging, and turn on two-step verification.

cards.title: Check who else is signed in
cards.body: Run the account check in this app. Spyware is often paired with someone logged into your accounts, so look for sessions, linked devices and mail forwarding you didn't set up.

cards.title: Call your bank on a number you trust
cards.body: If money or your SIM may be at risk, call your bank or operator using the number on your card or their official app — never a number from the message that worried you.

cards.title: Turn off call forwarding
cards.body: If your calls or texts are being forwarded, your codes could be reaching someone else. Use the forwarding check in this app to see and cancel it, then tell your operator.
